# Weak-RF response {.unnumbered #weak-rf-response}

## RF drive convention {#rf-drive-convention}

The RF Hamiltonian is

$$
\frac{H_{\mathrm{rf}}(t)}{\hbar}
=\Omega_{\mathrm{rf}}F_i\cos(\omega t).
$$

The real cosine contains positive- and negative-frequency components. Both co-rotating and counter-rotating responses are retained.

## Adjacent-coherence response {#adjacent-coherence-response}

For (|a\rangle=|F,m\rangle) and (|b\rangle=|F,m-1\rangle), the positive-frequency coefficient per unit RF Rabi frequency is

$$
\frac{\partial\rho_{ab,+}}{\partial\Omega_{\mathrm{rf}}}
=\frac{i(F_i)_{ab}(p_a-p_b)/2}
{\Gamma_{ab}+i(\omega_{ab}-\omega)}.
$$

The reverse ordered coherence supplies the counter-rotating denominator. An arbitrary Hermitian readout operator (O) gives

$$
\chi_+(\omega)=\sum_{a,b}O_{ba}
\frac{\partial\rho_{ab,+}}{\partial\Omega_{\mathrm{rf}}}.
$$

## Full resolvent {#rf-resolvent}

When coherence transfer must be retained, the solver uses

$$
\chi_+(\omega)=
\mathbf r^T(-i\omega I-G)^{-1}\mathbf s,
$$

where (G) is the coherence generator, (mathbf s) is the RF source, and (mathbf r) represents the selected readout.

## Phase components {#rf-phase-components}

The app reports

$$
X=2\operatorname{Re}\chi_+,
\qquad
Y=2\operatorname{Im}\chi_+,
\qquad
A=\sqrt{X^2+Y^2}.
$$

The factor of two reconstructs the real cosine response from its (e^{-i\omega t}) Fourier coefficient.

For a longer derivation, see the [weak-RF solver PDF](../rf_susceptibility_solver.pdf), its [LaTeX source](../rf_susceptibility_solver.tex), and the [frequency-convention note](../positive_negative_frequency_convention_v1.0.tex).
